newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bomb kills pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman.
newsitem.headline: Bomb kills pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman.

text.p: A pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman was killed in south Lebanon on Thursday by a bomb planted in his car by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas, South Lebanon Army (SLA) sources said.
The attack triggered heavy Israeli shelling which killed one Lebanese civilian and wounded two, security sources said.
In Beirut, a Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman claimed responsibility for the bombing.

"Hizbollah claims responsibility for this operation of the martyrs of Kfour," he said in reference to five Hizbollah guerrillas who were killed on Monday in Kfour in south Lebanon by roadside bombs planted by Israeli commandos.

SLA sources said one militiaman was killed in the car bomb attack which came one day after Hizbollah guerrillas fired more than 30 Katyusha rockets at the Israeli border. Pro-Israeli militia sources said there were no reports of casualties in the rocket attacks.
In a funeral procession on Tuesday for the Hizbollah fighters killed by the roadside bombs, the group threatened to unleash suicide bombings inside Israel and Arab land occupied by the Jewish state.

Hizbollah is fighting to drive some 1,000 Israeli troops and their local militia allies from a 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone in south Lebanon, site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and roadside bombs.
The latest violence came amid high Middle East tensions.

On Wednesday, Crown Prince Hassan of Jordan failed in Jerusalem talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to persuade Israel to lift sanctions imposed on Palestinians after two suicide bombers killed 13 people in a Jerusalem market last week.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said in remarks published on Thursday in an Israeli newspaper that measures imposed by the Jewish state against the Palestinians amounted to a declaration of war, and warned that he was preparing accordingly.
